prose_and_proof_audit: Price level, ordinary inflation, log inflation and annualization are separated; exact nominal/real dated gross factors precede first-order approximations. Expected reciprocal real returns are distinct from using expected inflation in a denominator.

Income velocity is defined for a matching final-output price/quantity pair, with stock/flow units and average money convention. Exact finite/log growth identities are separate from quantity-theory causal closure, money definition, endogenous velocity and one-time versus continuing changes.

Original pricing mechanism gives small firms an explicit global quadratic target; firms take aggregate p as given. Every log price uses100lnP. The geometric index and aggregate fixed-point algebra are explicit. The preset rule is assumed, not a silently optimized Calvo contract.

Only0<s<1 uses divided kappa/u formulas. Fully preset and fully resetting endpoints are derived from the undivided restriction, then closed by positive-b demand. The supplied reference output is not automatically the shock-specific natural level or a welfare benchmark.

Demand slope and nominal-expenditure implementation are maintained policy/spending restrictions. Unique simultaneous solution and all four shock derivatives are derived; model regimes and local extrapolation limits are explicit.

Adaptive prior-date forecasts update after realization; zero-shock and persistently forced affine recursions have exact contraction proofs and explicit lambda0, kappa0 and b0 scope boundaries. Finite log-gap sums are not confused with infinite sums, lost goods or welfare.

Model-consistent forecasts use finite conditional distributions and known model/regime, with nonzero realized forecast errors. Known versus surprise demand is a timing experiment, not a universal policy-ineffectiveness theorem. Prior-date current inflation differs from next-period expected inflation in c08.

Identification examples distinguish inflation-only ambiguity, expectation ambiguity even with output, mixed-shock descriptive OLS and an identified policy disturbance. No synthetic slope or shock is presented as an empirical estimate.

Three complete worked examples and eight full solutions independently recomputed, including exact compounding, matrix pricing, aggregation endpoints, disinflation paths, forecast distributions, slope reversal and policy critique. Teach-back and delayed check have explicit answers/criteria.

Three scoped primary methods were actually read; historical or current empirical assertions and numerical calibrations not established by those inspections are not imported. Both c08 successor mentions now link its existing manuscript.

resolved_authoring_issues.issue: Root requested uniform100lnP units, atomistic aggregate-price taking and separate preset-share endpoints.
resolved_authoring_issues.resolution: All are explicit before the divided Phillips equation; the executable solves the undivided system.

resolved_authoring_issues.issue: C08 uses a shock-specific flexible-price output benchmark and forward forecast, whereas c07 uses a baseline reference path and prior-period forecast.
resolved_authoring_issues.resolution: Definitions and successor bridge distinguish these objects; no unchanged-potential inference is made from cost disturbances.
